companies.title: Company domains
companies.description: One company per line: a domain like amazon.com, a full url, or a Trustpilot profile address. A line that repeats is free, a line that is not a domain comes back as its own free row with the reason.

maxReviewsPerCompany.title: Max reviews per company
maxReviewsPerCompany.description: Reviews are sold per row, so this is the ceiling that protects your budget. An anonymous run reaches at most 920 reviews per company: 20 from the newest page plus five star listings of nine filtered pages each. 920 is the maximum, not a phrase.

maxPagesPerCompany.title: Max pages per star filter
maxPagesPerCompany.description: Trustpilot serves an anonymous visitor at most 10 pages per listing (page 11 answers with an empty list), so 10 is both the default and the maximum. A star listing is read from page 2, because its first page ignores the filter. Lower it to trade depth for speed.

stars.title: Star filters to read
stars.description: Which star listings to read. Empty means all five, and each of them has nine filtered pages of its own: that is what lifts the 200 review wall. [1] reads only the worst reviews, which is the usual way to hear the real complaint. A star listing is read from page 2: its first page ignores the filter when the address carries page=1, so every row here carries the bucket it really came from.

publishedAfter.title: Only reviews published after
publishedAfter.description: An ISO date, for example 2026-11-01. Older reviews are read and then dropped, and the row that reports the company counts them, so an incremental run is not charged for what it skips.

language.title: Only reviews in this language
language.description: A two letter language code, for example en. Empty means every language. Reviews in other languages are read and dropped without a charge.

maxCompanies.title: Max companies
maxCompanies.description: Every company costs a fresh browser navigation, so this is the other budget ceiling. Companies beyond it come back free with status NOT_CHECKED_LIMIT.

includeReplies.title: Include the company's answer
includeReplies.description: On, each review carries the company's public reply and its date when one exists. Turn it off for a leaner dataset.
